subject: Operator roster attestation and recent subprocessor additions
messages:
From: Lydia Marsh <lydia.marsh@safaricloud.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@safaricloud.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Operator roster attestation and recent subprocessor additions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking our RFP. As part of our Security & Procurement review (RFP SAF-2027-RFP-011) we need: a current operator/third-party roster (all subprocessors engaged for production inference and telemetry), and a short attestation that there have been no material subprocessor additions in the last 90 days or, if there have, a change notice and impact assessment.

Two clarifying asks:
- We require an explicit callout for any cloud operators or managed service partners that have administrative access to production (console or VM-level).
- Because we have EU data residency requirements, can you confirm whether you have any new operators in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 in the past quarter and whether you provide regional fallback playbooks?

Can you send the roster and a draft attestation by EOD Thursday (May 20)? If you prefer, we can take a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Marsh
Senior Procurement Manager, SafariCloud
[Attachment: Procurement_SOW_Template.pdf (pdf)]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Marsh <lydia.marsh@safaricloud.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator roster attestation and recent subprocessor additions

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear asks. We're happy to provide the roster and a short attestation.

What I'm sending now: a first-pass operator roster (aditya_operator_roster_v1.xlsx) that lists all known subprocessors used in production inference paths and control-plane services. High-level notes included in the sheet.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Administrative access: only our managed cloud partners (AWS and GCP for hosted customers) and our orchestration partner (CloudOpsCo) have documented admin access to portions of the control plane — details are in the roster.
- EU operators: we did not add any new EU-based operators in the past 90 days; our regional fallback plan for eu-west-1 is documented and I can surface the relevant section for you.

I attached the roster and a draft attestation (subprocessor_attestation_draft.pdf) to speed review. Also sharing a Drive link where we keep the public subprocessor page: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/subprocessor/SAF-2027-RFP-011

If it helps, I'd like to set a 30-min sync tomorrow at 11:00 PT to run through the roster and confirm any fine-grained access controls. Let me know if that works for your team.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: aditya_operator_roster_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: subprocessor_attestation_draft.pdf (pdf)]
From: Lydia Marsh <lydia.marsh@safaricloud.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@safaricloud.com>, security@ssg.safaricloud.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator roster attestation and recent subprocessor additions

Aditya — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups after a brief review of the spreadsheet:

- The roster looks complete at the high level but we need explicit confirmation in the attestation about CloudOpsCo's level of access (console admin vs API-limited).
- For EU fallback: we need the playbook excerpt that explains how you reroute inference and how KV cache invalidation is handled across regions (we'll validate with our infra team).
- Our security team would prefer attestation language that can be signed / DocuSigned by your legal counsel. Can you submit the attestation through DocuSign and include a named signatory?

Procurement is OK with the 30-min sync — can you do Thu May 20 at 11:00 PT? If yes, we'll send a calendar invite.

Lydia

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 07:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Operator roster attestation and recent subprocessor additions — action items

Team — looping you in on a SafariCloud procurement request (RFP SAF-2027-RFP-011). They asked for: (1) explicit wording on CloudOpsCo admin access level, (2) the EU fallback playbook excerpt (how we reroute inference and KV cache invalidation), and (3) a DocuSign-ready attestation signed by counsel.

Attaching my draft attestation for legal redline; Vivek can you confirm the eu cache invalidation steps we can include as a playbook excerpt (high-level only — no secrets). Laura, can you prepare a signatory-friendly attestation and flag any risky language. Monica, please prep a short bullet list for the customer on how we notify customers for subprocessor changes (policy + 30-day notice).

Meeting scheduled Thu May 20 11:00 PT with SafariCloud. Need your inputs before 10:30 PT so I can finalize notes.

Thanks — Aditya
[Attachment: subprocessor_attestation_draft.pdf]
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Operator roster attestation and recent subprocessor additions — action items

Aditya/Vivek/Monica — I redlined the attestation and prepared a clean signatory version. Main points:
- Confirmed: No material subprocessor additions in the last 90 days affecting production inference other than standard patching/maintenance vendors.
- Confirmed: Administrative access levels for CloudOpsCo are limited to orchestration APIs and do not include root console access to customer production nodes; that is documented in the attached roster.
- Confirmed: Primary cloud operators in production remain AWS (eu-west-1) and GCP (europe-west2) for your region; no new eu-based operators were onboarded in the quarter.
- Notice policy: we maintain a 30-day change-notice window for subprocessor changes; emergency patches are handled under our Incident Communication policy (CS will notify affected customers within 48 hours). Monica — see the short customer-friendly bullets in the last section of the attached doc.

I've attached: attestation_redline_v1.docx (redline) and attestation_final_for_signing.pdf (clean signatory text). I'll route the final through DocuSign once Aditya confirms the customer wants counsel-signed attestation.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: attestation_redline_v1.docx (document)]
